name: Veterinary clinics and animal-health suppliers

problems.words: Reception phone and WhatsApp don't stop, we miss bookings
quick_ideas: Put bookings on one channel the whole team can see
Answer common questions (hours, location, services) where clients look first.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp booking assistant that takes requests by service, confirms them and passes them to reception, around the clock.

problems.ask_first: How do clients book with you now?
problems.free_stops: What the assistant handles and when it hands over stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many booking requests were missed or answered late in one busy day, so the reception bottleneck is clear.
Give one person each shift the job of writing every booking request in one paper list, so fewer appointments slip away.

problems.words: Pet owners forget boosters and we don't remind them
quick_ideas: Keep due dates in one list rather than in paper files
Remind the next week's clients, with their permission.

workzap_build.text: booking_scheduling — booster and recheck reminders sent automatically from the due dates the clinic enters.

problems.ask_first: Where are due dates kept today?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and wording are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many booster due dates passed last week without any reminder sent, so the missed repeat workload is clear.
Give one receptionist a fixed weekly time to check the due list and send reminders, so boosters stop being overlooked.

quick_ideas: Confirm surgery bookings the day before
Keep a short list of clients who can come in at short notice.

workzap_build.text: appointment reminders and confirmations sent automatically, with freed slots offered to the waiting list.

problems.ask_first: How far ahead are surgeries booked?
problems.free_stops: The reminder sequence and waiting-list flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many surgery slots sat unused after no-shows last week, so the cost of empty theatre time is clearer.
Keep one short-notice standby list in one place at reception, so cancelled surgery time is easier to refill.

problems.words: Vaccines lost when the fridge failed over the weekend
quick_ideas: Make one person responsible for checking the fridge out of hours
Ask your equipment supplier about a temperature alarm.

workzap_build.text: custom_build — fridge temperature alerts from a sensor routed to on-call staff, with every incident logged.

problems.ask_first: How would you find out today if the fridge failed on a Sunday?
problems.free_stops: Sensor connection and alert routing are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each weekend fridge interruption and what stock was discarded afterward, so the owner sees which failures are causing real wastage.
Give one staff member one weekend fridge incident notebook, so every power cut and stock loss is handed over on Monday.

problems.words: Medicines expire on the shelf because nobody checks dates
quick_ideas: Do one shelf check for near-expiry stock
Put the soonest-expiring items at the front.

workzap_build.text: a pharmacy stock list with batch and expiry dates and near-expiry alerts sent automatically.

problems.free_stops: Alert timing and stock setup stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many medicine packs expire within the next month on one shelf walk, so the scale of avoidable waste is obvious.
Give one assistant the date-check notebook for all shelves every week, so near-expiry stock gets noticed in time.

problems.words: Assistants give medicines without billing them
quick_ideas: Make it a rule that nothing leaves before it's on the bill
Check a few fast-moving items against bills each week, openly.

workzap_build.text: a billing checklist linking each consultation to items used, with daily stock-vs-bills gaps flagged automatically.

problems.ask_first: Is there one dispensing point or several?
problems.free_stops: How items link to bills is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count one day's medicine packs leaving the dispensary against that day's entries at the counter, so unpaid handouts stand out quickly.
Give one counter person one daily exceptions list for medicine handouts without entries, so each mismatch is checked before closing.

problems.words: Farm clients take visits and medicine on credit, months behind
quick_ideas: Send each farm client a statement of what's owed
Set your own credit limit per farm.

workzap_build.text: a farm client ledger with statements and reminders sent automatically.

problems.ask_first: How many farm clients buy on credit?
problems.free_stops: Statement layout and reminder rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many farm accounts have had no payment this season and note which are oldest, so follow-up time goes to the slowest payers.
Give one staff member one weekly farm dues notebook, so every reminder and reply stays together for the owner to review.

problems.words: Vets in the field don't log every visit, so we don't bill it
quick_ideas: Ask field vets to report each visit the same day
Match visits to invoices every week.

workzap_build.text: a field-visit form on the phone where each visit, items used and travel would be logged and the invoice would go out by WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: How many vets go on farm calls?
problems.free_stops: The visit log and invoicing flow stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one week's field visit notes with the invoices raised from those days, so missed chargeable work is easier to spot.
Give one clinic staff member one daily field visit list from returning vets, so each visit reaches the billing desk the same day.

problems.words: Google reviews complain about waiting time
quick_ideas: Tell clients the expected wait when they arrive
Reply calmly to each review.

workzap_build.text: real clients asked for a review automatically after their visit, so feedback reflects everyone, not just the unhappy few.

problems.ask_first: What do unhappy clients mention most?
problems.free_stops: The timing and flow of review requests go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the actual wait from arrival to consultation for several clients in one day, so the longest delay point stands out.
Give one receptionist the job of updating the waiting list in one place, so clients hear realistic delays before frustration grows.

problems.words: Weekend and night emergency rota causes fights
quick_ideas: Publish the rota well in advance so swaps are visible
Agree one fair rule for weekends.

workzap_build.text: a rota planner that spreads night and weekend cover and sends shift reminders automatically.

problems.ask_first: How many vets share the rota?
problems.free_stops: The rota rules and swap process are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note who covered each weekend and night over the past month, so the fairness problem stops being argued from memory.
Give one senior person the rota swap log in one notebook, so weekend cover arguments have a clear handover point.

never_say: Any diagnosis, treatment, dosing, prescribing or drug advice, even to a vet asking.
Anything on drug scheduling, prescription rules or registration.
Anything that helps sell unregistered, smuggled, expired or restricted medicines, relabel stock or falsify controlled-drug records.
Fake or incentivised reviews; review requests go only to real clients.
Storing pet owners' or farmers' personal details or medical record contents in pi's notes.

sample_reply.person: I run a small-animal clinic in Dubai with two vets. Clients keep forgetting vaccine boosters and then blame us. Can you help?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, move due dates out of paper files into one list the team can see.
Second, each week, remind the clients who are due, with their permission.
The next step up would be: booster and recheck reminders sent on WhatsApp from the due dates you enter, with bookings passed straight to reception.

Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you, or would you rather not?
